variants.title: Run the parsing pipeline
variants.context: Parsing runs as five staged layers: intake at the trust boundary, render and transcribe, recover layout, build evidence, then validate and release. Each layer can fail on its own, so each one runs in order and hands the next one source coordinates and parser identity.
variants.prompt: A tenant uploads a PDF to an extraction service. Put the pipeline stages in order, starting at the trust boundary.

items.text: Join tokens into blocks, cells, fields, and sections while retaining bounding boxes and confidence.
Detect regions, reading order, headings, lists, tables, figures, and repeated page furniture.
Read a trustworthy text layer where one exists, and render pages plus OCR only where text is absent or unreliable.
Apply typed rules, cross-field reconciliation, review policy, and destination release gates.
Verify type, size, encryption, malware status, tenant, and retention policy before rendering anything.

variants.hint: Which stage is allowed to touch the file first?
variants.explanation: Intake is a trust boundary, so file safety and tenant policy are settled before any page is rendered.

variants.title: Run the parsing pipeline
variants.context: Parsing runs as five staged layers: intake at the trust boundary, render and transcribe, recover layout, build evidence, then validate and release. Each layer can fail on its own, so each one runs in order and hands the next one source coordinates and parser identity.
variants.prompt: A born-digital two column report arrives with a reliable native text layer. Put the stages in order for that route.

items.text: Spans are joined into blocks, table cells, and sections, each keeping its bounding box.
Native spans and their coordinates are read instead of running OCR over rendered pages.
Deterministic validators run and the record is released to its destination.
Intake confirms the file type, size, and tenant, and that the document is not encrypted.
Region detection resolves the two columns into a single correct reading order.

variants.hint: A native text layer changes the transcription step, not the order of the stages.
variants.explanation: Native extraction replaces OCR inside the transcribe stage, but layout, evidence, and validation still run after it.

variants.title: Run the parsing pipeline
variants.context: Parsing runs as five staged layers: intake at the trust boundary, render and transcribe, recover layout, build evidence, then validate and release. Each layer can fail on its own, so each one runs in order and hands the next one source coordinates and parser identity.
variants.prompt: A scanned handwritten claim form has no text layer at all. Put the stages in order for that route.

items.text: Labels are linked to values with their field geometry and per-token confidence retained.
Pages are rendered and handwriting recognition transcribes them because no text layer exists.
Typed rules and review policy decide whether the record is released or held.
Intake screens the upload for malware and applies the tenant retention policy.
Regions and field boxes are detected and repeated page furniture is suppressed.

variants.hint: Missing text does not let the pipeline skip a stage; it changes how one stage is done.
variants.explanation: Every route runs the same five stages; the document shape only changes the work inside render and transcribe.

variants.title: Rebuild a table
variants.context: A table is a graph of cells and headers, not lines of whitespace. The lesson reconstructs it by finding the table region, inferring rows, columns and spans, attaching headers, then reconciling the result before records are produced.
variants.prompt: A borderless table sits between a caption and a neighboring column of body text. Put the reconstruction steps in order.

items.text: Propose a cell graph from whitespace, alignment, and token positions because no ruling lines exist.
Separate the table from the caption and the neighboring column, keeping its page coordinates.
Resolve which row and column headers govern each proposed cell.
Check column types, expected keys, and source coverage, and hold the result if the grid stays ambiguous.

variants.hint: Which step can only be done once the cell graph exists?
variants.explanation: Detection, structure, semantics, then validation: headers cannot be attached before there are cells to attach them to.

variants.title: Rebuild a table
variants.context: A table is a graph of cells and headers, not lines of whitespace. The lesson reconstructs it by finding the table region, inferring rows, columns and spans, attaching headers, then reconciling the result before records are produced.
variants.prompt: A ledger table runs across four pages with repeated headers and a carried total. Put the reconstruction steps in order.

items.text: Reconcile the carried total against the line items before emitting records.
Attach the repeated headers and stitch the continuation rows into one logical table.
Locate the table region on each page and record its coordinates separately per page.
Infer rows, columns, and spans on each page from borders and token positions.

variants.hint: Continuation is a header and semantics problem, not a detection problem.
variants.explanation: Multi-page tables are joined at the header step, and only the reconciled total proves the stitch was correct.

variants.title: Rebuild a table
variants.context: A table is a graph of cells and headers, not lines of whitespace. The lesson reconstructs it by finding the table region, inferring rows, columns and spans, attaching headers, then reconciling the result before records are produced.
variants.prompt: A financial statement uses merged cells and a two level header where one label governs three columns. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Verify the expected row count and that every value maps to exactly one header path.
Isolate the statement table from the surrounding figures and footnotes.
Resolve the stacked header levels and the units each governing label carries.
Propose cells and record the spans where one cell covers several columns.

variants.hint: Spans belong to the structure step; what they mean belongs to the next one.
variants.explanation: Recording a span is structure; deciding which stacked label governs it is semantics, and only validation proves the mapping.

variants.title: Match the route to the document
variants.context: There is no universally best parser. The route depends on whether a reliable text layer exists, how complex the page geometry is, which relationships carry meaning, and what happens after extraction. Spend OCR and vision capacity only where they recover evidence the product contract needs.
variants.prompt: A nightly intake receives one bundle per email: scanned receipts, a born-digital statement, and a handwritten note, all in one file. Which route should the service take?
options: Split the attachments, classify the page families, and send each family through its own measured route.
Rasterize every page and run the full OCR and vision route over the whole bundle.
Read the native text layer for the whole bundle and skip rendering entirely.
optionFeedback: Correct: a mixed bundle is classified and routed per page family instead of one expensive universal path.
This spends OCR and vision capacity on pages whose native text is already reliable.
The scanned receipts and the handwritten note have no usable text layer, so those pages would come back empty.
variants.hint: What does a bundle contain that a single route cannot serve well?
variants.explanation: Mixed bundles are split and classified first so each page family gets a route sized to the evidence it needs.

variants.title: Match the route to the document
variants.context: There is no universally best parser. The route depends on whether a reliable text layer exists, how complex the page geometry is, which relationships carry meaning, and what happens after extraction. Spend OCR and vision capacity only where they recover evidence the product contract needs.
variants.prompt: A ninety page annual report is born-digital but has columns, floating figures, marginalia, and multi-level tables that feed a search index and a metrics pipeline. Which route fits?
options: Take native spans only and emit them in file order as a plain text dump.
Combine native text with rendered-page layout detection, table structure, and section hierarchy.
Deskew and denoise the pages, then run OCR over every page as a scanned document.
optionFeedback: File order is not reading order here, and a text dump destroys the table relationships the metrics pipeline needs.
Correct: complex geometry with meaningful tables calls for the hybrid route across native text and layout models.
The report already has a trustworthy text layer, so OCR adds substitution risk and cost for no recovered evidence.
variants.hint: Which layer of evidence does this document have plenty of, and which one is still missing?
variants.explanation: Native text is available but geometry and structure are not, so the hybrid route adds layout and table modeling on top of it.

variants.title: Match the route to the document
variants.context: There is no universally best parser. The route depends on whether a reliable text layer exists, how complex the page geometry is, which relationships carry meaning, and what happens after extraction. Spend OCR and vision capacity only where they recover evidence the product contract needs.
variants.prompt: A claims team submits photographed forms: skewed, some fields handwritten, and the downstream system needs each answer tied to its field box. Which route fits?
options: Extract whatever native spans the camera app embedded and treat those as the record.
Deskew, detect regions, run recognition, and keep the geometry of every field.
Detect table structure first and read the form as rows and columns of a grid.
optionFeedback: A photograph has no trustworthy text layer, so anything embedded by the camera app is not evidence.
Correct: a scanned form is a vision-first route where field geometry has to survive into the record.
A form carries label to value links, not row and column relationships, so grid structure is the wrong model.
variants.hint: Which relationship carries the meaning in a form?
variants.explanation: Forms are vision-first and their meaning lives in label to value links, so field geometry must be preserved.

variants.title: Gate before the action
variants.context: Confidence is a model estimate, not proof of correctness. A parser can be highly confident about the wrong digit, so deterministic checks such as subtotal reconciliation, currency parsing, and identifier checksums catch a different class of failure. Gate the specific fields an action depends on, and keep a review path.
variants.prompt: An invoice total is extracted with 0.97 confidence, but the line items sum to a different figure. The record would trigger a payment. What should the gate do?
options: Hold it for review, because reconciliation failed even though confidence is high.
Lower the threshold for this vendor so the reconciliation warning stops firing.
Release it, because 0.97 clears the configured confidence threshold for this field.
optionFeedback: Correct: a deterministic reconciliation failure is evidence of a real inconsistency and blocks the action.
Tuning the threshold hides the contradiction instead of resolving it, and payment still fires on a bad total.
Confidence is a model estimate, and a parser can be highly confident about the wrong digit.
variants.hint: Which of these two signals is proof rather than an estimate?
variants.explanation: Deterministic checks catch a different class of failure than confidence, so a failed reconciliation must fail closed.

variants.title: Gate before the action
variants.context: Confidence is a model estimate, not proof of correctness. A parser can be highly confident about the wrong digit, so deterministic checks such as subtotal reconciliation, currency parsing, and identifier checksums catch a different class of failure. Gate the specific fields an action depends on, and keep a review path.
variants.prompt: A team gates automated payment on one aggregate document confidence score averaged across all extracted fields. What is the flaw?
options: The average can stay high while the exact fields the payment depends on are wrong.
The average is cheap to compute but slow to update after a parser change.
The average is only valid when every field on the page has the same parser version.
optionFeedback: Correct: a page of correct addresses can carry a wrong amount and still average well above the threshold.
Cost and refresh latency are not why the gate lets a bad payment through.
Version consistency belongs in the identity record and is not what breaks this gate.
variants.hint: What does the payment actually depend on, and what is the score measuring?
variants.explanation: Gate the specific fields and relationships the action depends on, never one aggregate score for the whole document.

variants.title: Gate before the action
variants.context: Confidence is a model estimate, not proof of correctness. A parser can be highly confident about the wrong digit, so deterministic checks such as subtotal reconciliation, currency parsing, and identifier checksums catch a different class of failure. Gate the specific fields an action depends on, and keep a review path.
variants.prompt: The same parser output feeds a full-text search index and a clinical record update. How should the release gates be set?
options: Use one gate tuned to the clinical path so the search index inherits the same safety.
Use one gate tuned to the search path so review load stays low on both destinations.
Use a separate gate per destination, because they tolerate different errors.
optionFeedback: A clinical threshold applied to search buries recoverable documents and wastes review capacity for no benefit.
A search threshold applied to clinical data lets an unverified value reach a patient record.
Correct: the lesson gates by what happens after extraction, and search and clinical use have different error costs.
variants.hint: What changes between the two destinations, the extraction or its consequences?
variants.explanation: Release thresholds belong to the destination: search indexing tolerates errors that a clinical or payment path cannot.

variants.title: Locate the failing stage
variants.context: Measure each stage separately: transcription accuracy, region detection and reading order, table and form structure, and the business field outcome. A good OCR score can coexist with broken reading order or incorrect table relationships, so a symptom points at one stage.
variants.prompt: Match each observed symptom to the evaluation stage that exposes it most directly.

pairs.label: Transcription
pairs.detail: Word error rate is fine on printed pages but collapses on the handwriting slice.

pairs.label: Regions and order
pairs.detail: Two columns are read as one interleaved stream even though every word is correct.

pairs.label: Tables and forms
pairs.detail: A stacked header attaches to the wrong column, so values land under the wrong label.

pairs.label: Fields
pairs.detail: Values are exact, but a released record carries no link back to the page region that supports it.

variants.hint: Ask which layer of evidence the symptom breaks, not which one is easiest to measure.
variants.explanation: Stages are scored separately because a strong score at one layer says nothing about the layer above it.

variants.title: Locate the failing stage
variants.context: Measure each stage separately: transcription accuracy, region detection and reading order, table and form structure, and the business field outcome. A good OCR score can coexist with broken reading order or incorrect table relationships, so a symptom points at one stage.
variants.prompt: A regression lands after a parser upgrade. Match each report from operations to the stage that exposes it.

pairs.label: Transcription
pairs.detail: Character error rate rises only for one language on low quality scans.

pairs.label: Regions and order
pairs.detail: A repeated page footer is now emitted as body text in the middle of a section.

pairs.label: Tables and forms
pairs.detail: A continuation row on page three is dropped when the repeated header reappears.

pairs.label: Fields
pairs.detail: Review load doubles while exact value accuracy stays flat.

variants.hint: Page furniture and reading order belong to the same layer.
variants.explanation: Each symptom names one stage, so measuring stages separately turns a vague regression into a located one.

variants.title: Locate the failing stage
variants.context: Measure each stage separately: transcription accuracy, region detection and reading order, table and form structure, and the business field outcome. A good OCR score can coexist with broken reading order or incorrect table relationships, so a symptom points at one stage.
variants.prompt: You are building the evaluation set partitions. Match each measurement to the stage it belongs to.

pairs.label: Transcription
pairs.detail: Character and word error by language, scan quality, and font.

pairs.label: Regions and order
pairs.detail: Region detection, reading order, hierarchy, and page furniture suppression.

pairs.label: Tables and forms
pairs.detail: Cell adjacency, header association, spans, key-value links, and continuation.

pairs.label: Fields
pairs.detail: Exact values, provenance coverage, reconciliation, and escaped error cost.

variants.hint: One of these stages is the only one that measures a business outcome.
variants.explanation: The four stages measure text, geometry, structure, and business outcome, and the evaluation set is partitioned to cover all four.
